species.description: A holoparasite with no stem, leaves or roots of its own, living entirely inside the tissue of Tetrastigma vines and emerging only to flower. Among the largest single flowers in the world, reaching about one metre across.
species.characteristics: No chlorophyll. Visible only as a cabbage-like bud for up to nine months before opening; the open flower lasts four to six days and smells of carrion, which attracts the flies that pollinate it.
species.leaf_description: None. The vegetative body is a thread-like network of filaments inside the host vine.
species.flower_description: Five thick brick-red lobes covered in pale warts, surrounding a deep central chamber with a raised disk bearing spiny processes. Unisexual.
species.fruit_description: A woody berry to 15 cm across holding thousands of minute seeds in a sticky pulp, probably dispersed by tree shrews and ground squirrels.
species.habitat: Primary and old secondary lowland and hill dipterocarp forest, on shaded slopes where its Tetrastigma host is established.
species.distribution: Endemic to Borneo; recorded in Sarawak at Gunung Gading, Sri Aman and scattered hill forest sites.

species.description: A pitcher plant that has largely given up trapping insects. It forms dense carpets of squat ground pitchers that collect and digest falling leaf litter, making it partly detritivorous.
species.characteristics: Rosettes of ground pitchers spread across the forest floor from creeping stems; upper pitchers are sparse or absent. Pitcher fluid hosts a whole community of mosquito larvae, midges and frogs.
species.leaf_description: Lanceolate, 8-25 cm long, tapering into a tendril that swells into the pitcher.
species.flower_description: Small reddish-brown flowers in a branched panicle to 40 cm; plants are dioecious.
species.fruit_description: A dry capsule splitting into four valves, releasing thread-like wind-borne seeds.
species.habitat: Peat swamp forest, kerangas (heath forest) and damp shaded sites on sandy soil.
species.distribution: Borneo, Sumatra, Peninsular Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and New Guinea. Common across lowland Sarawak.

species.description: A highly variable climbing pitcher plant with strikingly dimorphic traps: bulbous speckled lower pitchers and slender funnel-shaped upper pitchers carried high in the canopy.
species.characteristics: Lower pitchers sit on the ground with two fringed wings; upper pitchers hang from tendrils and are wingless. Colour ranges from pale green to deep maroon speckling.
species.leaf_description: Leathery, oblong-lanceolate to 40 cm, with a prominent midrib extending into the tendril.
species.flower_description: Racemes to 70 cm of small reddish flowers, strongly scented at night in some forms.
species.fruit_description: Capsule 15-30 mm, four-valved, with numerous thread-like seeds.
species.habitat: Kerangas, peat swamp margins, coastal scrub and disturbed open ground on poor sandy soils.
species.distribution: Borneo, Sumatra, Peninsular Malaysia and Singapore. Widespread in the Sarawak lowlands.

species.description: One of the densest and most durable timbers in the world. Belian sinks in water, resists termites and marine borers, and standing trees can exceed a thousand years of age.
species.characteristics: Extremely slow growing. Heartwood darkens from yellow to near black on exposure. Heavily logged for shingles, bridges and house posts, and now protected in Sarawak.
species.leaf_description: Alternate, elliptic to oblong, 10-20 cm, leathery, glossy dark green above with a pale underside; the young flush is bright red.
species.flower_description: Small yellowish-green flowers in short axillary panicles, faintly scented.
species.fruit_description: A very large ovoid drupe 10-18 cm long with a thick woody shell, the largest fruit in the laurel family. Dispersed by gravity and by bearded pigs.
species.habitat: Lowland mixed dipterocarp forest on well-drained clay and sandy soils, often along ridges and riverbanks below 500 m.
species.distribution: Borneo, Sumatra, Palawan and the southern Philippines. Widespread but heavily depleted in Sarawak.

species.description: The principal source of illipe nut, an oil-rich seed harvested by Iban and other communities and exported as a cocoa butter substitute. Masts irregularly, at intervals of three to seven years.
species.characteristics: Fast growing for a dipterocarp and widely planted along rivers. Bole to 40 m with pale grey, shallowly fissured bark and clear resin.
species.leaf_description: Large, oblong to elliptic, 15-35 cm, with 14-20 pairs of parallel secondary veins; stipules conspicuous on young shoots.
species.flower_description: Cream to pale yellow, fragrant, borne in axillary panicles during mast years.
species.fruit_description: A nut about 4 cm enclosed by three long and two short wings, spinning as it falls. Seeds are recalcitrant and must be sown within days.
species.habitat: Alluvial flats and riverbanks in lowland mixed dipterocarp forest, tolerant of seasonal flooding.
species.distribution: Endemic to Borneo, chiefly Sarawak and West Kalimantan; widely planted in agroforestry.

species.description: An emergent giant to 65 m, historically the source of Borneo camphor, once traded to China at a higher price than gold. Famous for crown shyness, where neighbouring canopies never quite touch.
species.characteristics: Crystalline camphor forms in cavities in the trunk of old trees. Timber is sold as kapur. Populations have collapsed through logging across the range.
species.leaf_description: Ovate to lanceolate, 6-12 cm, glossy, with a finely pointed tip, aromatic when crushed.
species.flower_description: White, fragrant, about 2 cm across, in short axillary racemes.
species.fruit_description: A nut seated in a cup, with five long strap-shaped wings to 10 cm that autorotate in the wind.
species.habitat: Well-drained sandy or loamy soils in lowland dipterocarp forest, often gregarious and forming near pure stands.
species.distribution: Borneo, Sumatra and Peninsular Malaysia. In Sarawak now restricted to protected and remnant forest.

species.description: Among the tallest tropical trees, reaching 85 m with a smooth pale trunk and enormous buttresses. Culturally protected because giant honey bees nest in its limbs.
species.characteristics: The slippery bark deters bears and other climbers, which is why Apis dorsata colonies favour it. Felling a tapang is taboo in many Iban communities and the tree is legally protected in Sarawak.
species.leaf_description: Pinnate with 5-9 alternate leaflets, each 3-8 cm, leathery and blunt-tipped.
species.flower_description: Small greenish-white flowers massed in axillary panicles, attracting large numbers of bees.
species.fruit_description: A flat, thin, winged pod 8-15 cm containing a single seed, dispersed by wind from great height.
species.habitat: Lowland mixed dipterocarp forest on well-drained soils, typically as a scattered emergent.
species.distribution: Borneo, Sumatra, Peninsular Malaysia, Thailand and the Philippines.

species.description: A peat swamp timber tree, pale and even-grained, so heavily traded that it was listed on CITES Appendix II. Regeneration is poor wherever peat has been drained or burned.
species.characteristics: Slender bole to 30 m with stilt-like lower buttresses. Depends on intact waterlogged peat; drainage for plantations is the main threat.
species.leaf_description: Alternate, elliptic, 6-14 cm, glossy above with fine parallel veins and a drip tip.
species.flower_description: Small greenish-cream flowers in terminal panicles.
species.fruit_description: A three-lobed woody capsule 3-5 cm opening to expose seeds with an orange aril taken by hornbills.
species.habitat: Deep ombrogenous peat swamp forest, usually where peat exceeds one metre.
species.distribution: Borneo, Sumatra and Peninsular Malaysia. Sarawak peat swamps hold a significant share of what remains.

species.description: A conifer among tropical broadleaf giants, with a straight columnar trunk and flaking bark that bleeds copious white resin, once collected as the copal of commerce.
species.characteristics: One of very few native conifers in Borneo. Resin was traded for varnish and torches. Slow to regenerate after logging.
species.leaf_description: Opposite, leathery, elliptic to oblong, 5-12 cm, with no midrib and many fine parallel veins, unusual for a conifer.
species.flower_description: Not flowering. Male cones cylindrical 2-5 cm; female cones globose on short stout stalks.
species.fruit_description: A near-spherical cone 6-10 cm that disintegrates on the tree, releasing winged seeds.
species.habitat: Kerangas and peat swamp margins on poor acidic sandy soils, and on ridge crests.
species.distribution: Borneo, Sumatra, Peninsular Malaysia and the Philippines.

species.description: A stemless understorey palm whose leaf is a single pleated disc up to a metre across, undivided and almost perfectly circular, one of the most distinctive plants in Sarawak.
species.characteristics: Endemic to Sarawak and much sought after by collectors, which is the main pressure on wild populations. Grows very slowly in deep shade.
species.leaf_description: Orbicular, entire, pleated, 60-100 cm across, held on a slender spiny petiole 1-2 m long.
species.flower_description: Small cream flowers on a slender branched inflorescence shorter than the leaves.
species.fruit_description: Globose, 8-12 mm, ripening orange to red, taken by ground birds.
species.habitat: Deeply shaded understorey of lowland mixed dipterocarp forest on humid clay slopes and stream banks.
species.distribution: Endemic to western Sarawak, mainly the Kuching and Sri Aman divisions.

species.description: A jackfruit relative bearing a strongly fragrant fruit with soft white segments, widely regarded as one of the finest fruits of Borneo.
species.characteristics: All parts exude white latex. Cultivated in village orchards throughout Sarawak and Sabah as well as growing wild.
species.leaf_description: Very large, to 50 cm, obovate, three-lobed on juvenile shoots, rough above and hairy below.
species.flower_description: Unisexual heads on the same tree; male heads club-shaped, female heads globose.
species.fruit_description: A syncarp 15-20 cm covered in soft green bristles, opening to reveal sweet white perianth segments around each seed.
species.habitat: Lowland forest and village orchards on well-drained soils below 1000 m.
species.distribution: Native to Borneo and Palawan; cultivated across island Southeast Asia.

species.description: A wild durian with vivid orange to crimson flesh and a mild, nutty scent far gentler than the common durian. Increasingly planted as a specialty fruit.
species.characteristics: Bat-pollinated, with flowers opening at dusk. One of several wild Durio species in Borneo that are important genetic resources for the cultivated crop.
species.leaf_description: Alternate, oblong, 10-20 cm, dark green above with a dense coppery-scaly underside that flashes in the wind.
species.flower_description: Golden to reddish, borne on the trunk and larger branches, opening in the evening for nectar-feeding bats.
species.fruit_description: Ovoid, 12-18 cm, with short broad pyramidal spines, splitting on the tree to show orange or red arils.
species.habitat: Lowland and hill mixed dipterocarp forest to about 1000 m, often on sandy or loamy ridges.
species.distribution: Borneo, Sumatra and Peninsular Malaysia; widely grown in Sarawak smallholdings.

species.description: A robust clumping ginger to 6 m whose waxy pink inflorescence rises on its own leafless stalk directly from the rhizome. The flower bud is a staple of Southeast Asian cooking.
species.characteristics: Forms large colonies from creeping rhizomes. Buds are used in laksa and sambal; the plant is equally common as an ornamental hedge.
species.leaf_description: Lanceolate, to 80 cm, arranged in two ranks along tall reed-like pseudostems.
species.flower_description: A torch-like head 10-15 cm of glossy pink to red bracts on a stalk 1-1.5 m tall, arising separately from the leafy shoots.
species.fruit_description: A crowded head of reddish hairy capsules holding small black seeds in white pulp.
species.habitat: Damp forest edges, stream banks, cultivated ground and village plots in full to partial sun.
species.distribution: Native to Southeast Asia and naturalised widely; common throughout Sarawak.

species.description: A fast-growing pioneer shrub of roadsides and wet open ground, with large yellow flowers that last a single morning and star-shaped fruits that split at dawn.
species.characteristics: The big leaves are traditionally used to wrap tempeh and market food. Colonises disturbed and waterlogged land quickly, which makes it useful for restoration screening.
species.leaf_description: Broadly obovate, 15-30 cm, thick, with a strongly corrugated surface and prominent parallel side veins.
species.flower_description: Bright yellow, 8-12 cm across, with five crumpled petals and a dense boss of stamens; open for one morning only.
species.fruit_description: A star-shaped follicle opening at first light into pink-red segments with blue-black seeds in scarlet arils, taken immediately by birds.
species.habitat: Wet secondary scrub, roadside ditches, swamp margins and abandoned land in full sun.
species.distribution: Borneo, Sumatra, Peninsular Malaysia and Singapore; abundant across lowland Sarawak.

species.description: The most valuable small-diameter rattan in the region, producing a pale, even, flexible cane that is the standard raw material for quality furniture binding.
species.characteristics: Clustering, climbing to 40 m by whip-like flagella armed with recurved hooks. Heavily harvested from the wild; now also planted under forest canopy.
species.leaf_description: Pinnate to 1.5 m, with regularly arranged narrow leaflets and a spiny sheath bearing a long grapnel-tipped cirrus.
species.flower_description: Dioecious, on slender branched inflorescences emerging from the leaf sheaths.
species.fruit_description: Rounded, about 1 cm, covered in neat overlapping whitish scales, with a single seed.
species.habitat: Lowland dipterocarp and freshwater swamp forest, often on alluvial soils near rivers.
species.distribution: Borneo, Sumatra, Peninsular Malaysia and Palawan.

species.description: A shade-loving aroid with arrow-shaped leaves marked by bold silver-white veins against dark green, held stiffly upright on spotted petioles.
species.characteristics: Highly variable across its range with many named forms. Sap contains calcium oxalate crystals and irritates skin.
species.leaf_description: Arrow-shaped, 20-50 cm, dark green with silvery primary veins and a paler purplish underside.
species.flower_description: A pale green spathe enclosing a cream spadix, pollinated by drosophilid flies.
species.fruit_description: A cluster of orange-red berries exposed as the spathe withers.
species.habitat: Damp shaded understorey, stream banks and limestone bases in lowland and hill forest.
species.distribution: Borneo, Sumatra, Peninsular Malaysia, Java and Thailand.

species.description: A small Sarawak endemic begonia with asymmetric leaves patterned in bright green or silver spots over a near-black or deep red ground, known from very few localities.
species.characteristics: Restricted to shaded sandstone and limestone outcrops. Highly prized in cultivation, and wild collecting is a genuine threat to the small known populations.
species.leaf_description: Obliquely ovate, 6-12 cm, dark olive to blackish-red with scattered pale green spots and a red underside.
species.flower_description: White to pale pink, monoecious, in small cymes held just above the foliage.
species.fruit_description: A three-winged capsule with one wing longer than the others, releasing dust-fine seeds.
species.habitat: Deep shade on damp rock faces, cliff bases and stream gullies in lowland forest.
species.distribution: Endemic to Sarawak, known from a handful of sites in the Bau and Serian areas.

species.description: A medium-sized dipterocarp of riverbanks and lower slopes, yielding a hard heavy timber traded as resak and a clear dammar resin.
species.characteristics: Bark smooth to slightly scaly, grey-brown, exuding pale resin when cut. Populations fragmented by lowland clearance.
species.leaf_description: Elliptic to oblong, 8-18 cm, with distinctly raised fine net venation on the underside.
species.flower_description: Small, white to pale pink, fragrant, in short axillary panicles.
species.fruit_description: A nut 1-2 cm with two enlarged wings and three short lobes at the base.
species.habitat: Riverine and lower slope mixed dipterocarp forest on alluvium and clay, below 600 m.
species.distribution: Borneo, Sumatra and Peninsular Malaysia.

species.description: A very fast pioneer with huge shield-shaped leaves that dominates forest gaps, logging roads and abandoned farmland within a few years of disturbance.
species.characteristics: Hollow twigs of related species house Crematogaster ants in a classic ant-plant partnership. Short-lived, and normally displaced as primary forest species return.
species.leaf_description: Shield-shaped, broadly ovate, 30-60 cm across, shallowly three-lobed, whitish and hairy beneath.
species.flower_description: Dioecious; small yellowish flowers in large much-branched panicles.
species.fruit_description: A small two-lobed capsule covered in yellow resinous glands, with black seeds taken by bulbuls.
species.habitat: Forest gaps, landslips, logging roads, riverbanks and secondary growth in full sun.
species.distribution: Borneo, Sumatra, Peninsular Malaysia and Thailand; abundant in disturbed Sarawak lowlands.

species.description: A close relative of rambutan with a thicker dark red rind and short blunt tubercles rather than soft spines, and a sweeter flesh that separates cleanly from the seed.
species.characteristics: Grown in village orchards across Borneo and traded in local markets. Fruiting is seasonal and often follows a dry spell.
species.leaf_description: Pinnate with 2-5 pairs of elliptic leaflets, each 7-18 cm, glossy above and dull below.
species.flower_description: Small greenish-white flowers in terminal panicles, faintly scented.
species.fruit_description: Ellipsoid, 5-8 cm, dark red with thick blunt tubercles, the white aril sweet and free from the seed.
species.habitat: Lowland forest and cultivated orchards on well-drained soils below 500 m.
species.distribution: Native to Borneo, Sumatra and Peninsular Malaysia; widely cultivated.

species.description: Nepenthes gracilis, or the slender pitcher-plant, is a common lowland pitcher plant that is widespread in the Sunda region. It has been recorded from Borneo, Cambodia, Peninsular Malaysia, Singapore, Sulawesi, Sumatra, and Thailand. The species has a wide altitudinal distribution of 0 to 1,100 meters above sea level, although most populations are found below 100 meters and plants are rare above 1,000 meters. Despite being a widespread plant, natural hybrids between N. gracilis and other species are quite rare.

species.description: Asystasia intrusa, also known as African coromandel, is a species of flowering plant in the family Acanthaceae, first described in 1775 by Forsskal. It is a scrambling annual or subshrub that grows mainly in seasonally dry tropical regions. The species is native to large parts of Tropical and Southern Africa, the Arabian Peninsula, Madagascar, and nearby islands. It has also been introduced to parts of Asia and the Americas, including China, Taiwan, Costa Rica, and Venezuela.

species.description: Arundina graminifolia, also called bamboo orchid, is a species of orchid and the first sole accepted species of the genus Arundina, followed by A. caespitosa discovered in 2007. This tropical Asiatic genus extends from Myanmar, India, Sri Lanka, Nepal, Thailand, Vietnam, the Ryukyu Islands, Malaysia, Singapore, China to Indonesia, the Philippines and New Guinea. It has become naturalized in Réunion, Fiji, French Polynesia, Micronesia, the West Indies, Costa Rica, Panama, Belize, and Hawaii. There are medicinal benefits to utilizing components of Arundina graminifolia, including soothing, anti-inflammatory, anti-bacterial and anti-pain properties; frequently used in Chinese medicine.

species.description: Nepenthes veitchii, or Veitch's pitcher-plant, is a Nepenthes species from the island of Borneo. The plant is widespread in north-western Borneo and can also be found in parts of Kalimantan. It grows in lowland Dipterocarp forest, typically near rivers, and on ridgetops in mossy forests, from 0 to 1,600 meters elevation. Nepenthes veitchii usually grows as an epiphyte, though the form from Bario seems to be strictly terrestrial and has not been observed to climb trees.

species.description: Dipteris conjugata is a species of fern in the family Dipteridaceae. It has a rhizome, and 2-3 tall stems with mid green or dark green fronds, which have several divisions to toothed lobes. It is grows in clearings, mountain ridges and in forest margins, from tropical and temperate Asia, northern Queensland in Australia and some islands in the Pacific Ocean. It has limited native medicinal uses.

species.description: Melastoma malabathricum, known also as Malabar melastome, Indian rhododendron, Singapore rhododendron, planter's rhododendron and senduduk, is a flowering plant in the family Melastomataceae native to Seychelles, tropical and subtropical Asia to Australia and western Pacific islands. Despite its common names, it does not have any connection to actual rhododendrons, and belongs to the Rosids clade as opposed to the Asterids clade. This plant is usually found at elevations between 100 m and 2,800 m in grassland and sparse forest habitats. It has been used as a medicinal plant in certain parts of the world, but has been declared a noxious weed in the United States. M. malabathricum is a known hyperaccumulator of aluminium, and as such can be used for phytoremediation.

species.description: Mimosa pudica is a creeping annual or perennial flowering plant of the pea/legume family Fabaceae. It is often grown for its curiosity value: the sensitive compound leaves quickly fold inward and droop when touched or shaken and re-open a few minutes later. For this reason, this species is commonly cited as an example of rapid plant movement. Like a number of other plant species, it undergoes changes in leaf orientation termed "sleep" or nyctinastic movement. The foliage closes during darkness and reopens in light. This was first studied by French scientist Jean-Jacques d'Ortous. In the UK it has gained the Royal Horticultural Society's Award of Garden Merit.

species.description: Diospyros maingayi is a tree in the family Ebenaceae. It grows up to 30 metres (100 ft) tall. The twigs dry black. Inflorescences bear up to four flowers. The fruits are oblong to ellipsoid, up to 5 cm (2 in) long. The tree is named for British botanist A. C. Maingay. Habitat is peat swamp and other lowland forests. D. maingayi is found in Sumatra, Peninsular Malaysia and Borneo.

species.description: Passiflora foetida is a species of passion flower that is native to the southwestern United States, Mexico, the Caribbean, Central America, and much of South America. It has been introduced to tropical regions around the world, such as Southeast Asia, South Asia, Hawaii, Africa, and The Maldives. It is a creeping vine like other members of the genus, and yields an edible fruit. The specific epithet, foetida, means "stinking" in Latin and refers to the strong aroma emitted by damaged foliage.

species.description: Dischidia major, the Malayan urn vine, is a plant in the genus Dischidia. They carry modified leaves, offering accommodation to ants, including those of the family Dolichoderinae, and in return gain some sustenance from increased carbon dioxide and nitrogen levels, and a degree of protection from noxious animals and plants. This mutualism trait, known as myrmecophily, is widespread across the plant world and clearly carries considerable benefits for both ants and plant.
